clue.text: Planet almost consumed in flood

indicators.note: almost means the planet's name stops one letter short of complete

parts.note: Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun
consumed means ate, past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A cosmic disaster: a planet nearly swallowed up by a deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood something is to soak it completely with water, a direct synonym as verbs.

clue.text: Palace in cathedral city and diocese

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A palace located in a cathedral city and its diocese, as a bishop's palace would be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bishop's palace, but the palace is the French president's residence in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée is the official residence of the President of France in Paris.

clue.text: Bloke, hot, better going outside

indicators.note: going outside means the word for better wraps around the letter for hot

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man, warm and on the mend, heading out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as an adjective (recovered) but works as the verb cap, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British slang for a man or fellow, a synonym.

clue.text: First person caught in a far-off land

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
off means the letters of 'a far' are put wrong, rearranged into AFRA

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The narrator is trapped in some distant country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges 'a far' to AFRA, and IC is placed in its middle; 'in' signals that placement.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is a continent, a large land mass, so it is an example of a land.

clue.text: In or out

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the batter ... is the one facing the bowling, so is in
workers who have stopped work in protest are said to be out

explanation.surface: A tiny clue posing a choice between two opposites.
explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions look like opposites, yet the same phrase means both: a cricketer facing the bowling and a worker who has walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a batter facing deliveries in cricket and a worker withdrawing labour in a dispute.

clue.text: Ornament Celts originally placed under rocky hill

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed under another follows it

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the word Celts is used

explanation.surface: An ancient Celtic ornament buried beneath a craggy hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a neck ring of twisted metal worn as jewellery, an ornament, by Celts.

clue.text: Foreign coin to add in among Jamaican notes?

indicators.note: among means the pieces sit within the letters for the Jamaican music

parts.note: ska is a style of Jamaican music, so its notes
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A traveller adding a strange coin to a wallet of Jamaican banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes but means music, the Jamaican style ska.
explanation.definitionFit: The stotinka is a Bulgarian coin, a hundredth of a lev, so it is foreign money.

clue.text: Film director does repairs round house at last

indicators.note: round means the word for does repairs surrounds the other letter

parts.note: mends means does repairs

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of the word house is used

explanation.surface: A film director fixing up the area around a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Mendes is a British director of films such as American Beauty and 1917.

clue.text: Total entertainment — everything being enjoyed by blondes?

definitions.meaning: the phrase means every amusement on offer, the full experience
blondes are ...-haired, so the ... are enjoying everything fun

explanation.surface: A dumb-blonde joke: blondes get to have all the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'fair' as fair-haired people rather than a funfair; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the full range of excitement and amusement, as at a travelling funfair.

clue.text: See 9
Green, coup d'état his sin, taken out

indicators.note: taken out suggests something knocked about or dismantled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political plotter whose sin was a coup that was stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour or an environmentalist but means naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or naive, lacking worldly polish, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Archipelago, East Indian, with us all on the move

indicators.note: on the move means the letters travel around, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An Indian from the East joins everyone else on a journey to some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aleutian Islands are a chain of islands stretching west from Alaska, an archipelago.

clue.text: No good avoiding casual employment rates

indicators.note: avoiding means the letters for no good are left out

parts.note: temping is temporary, casual office work

explanation.surface: Low pay rates make casual work a bad deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed or rate at which music is played.

clue.text: Right on a length

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Something just right, judged on a length, like a well-pitched delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a cricket term: the leg side of the field is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means lawful, allowed by law, so right in the sense of permitted.

clue.text: Death tally back with hospital gone from local area

parts.note: death is an end

indicators.note: gone means the hospital letter is removed
back means the word for tally is read from right to left, giving EMIHC

parts.note: to tally is to agree or chime

explanation.surface: A local death count rises once the hospital closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tally' looks like a count but is the verb meaning agree; 'back' gives EMIHC, and 'gone' removes H to leave EMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic describes a disease or species native to a particular region, belonging there.

clue.text: Find dance almost dead

indicators.note: almost means the dance word loses its last letter

parts.note: a disco is a dance
over means finished, dead

explanation.surface: Discovering that a dance is nearly lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to find it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Skyline against one lake

parts.note: contra is Latin for against, used in English
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A city skyline set against a single lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skyline' reads as a horizon of buildings but is split as a line in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrail is the vapour trail left by an aircraft, literally a line across the sky.

clue.text: Appendix in the middle given serious cut

indicators.note: in the middle means the two central letters of the word Appendix are taken

parts.note: grave means serious

explanation.surface: A surgeon makes a serious incision to take out an appendix.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut letters or designs into a hard surface, so cut is a synonym.

clue.text: Service for example including meat, not the heart

indicators.note: including means the abbreviation for for example wraps around the rest
not the heart means the central letter of the meat is removed

parts.note: venison is deer meat

explanation.surface: A meal service, with meat on the menu but heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests the meal service the meat implies, but it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening service of prayer, a type of church service.

clue.text: Game in which loser first to take lead?

definitions.text: Game in which loser first to take lead?

parts.words: Game in which loser first to take lead?
parts.note: in this deadly game the loser is the first player to receive a bullet, lead, from the revolver

explanation.surface: A sporting paradox: the loser is the one who gets into the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests being in front but means bullet metal; 'take lead' is being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In the deadly game, players take turns firing a revolver holding one round at their own heads.

clue.text: Feel remorse having run over bird

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece over another comes first

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an egret is a heron-like wading bird

explanation.surface: A driver feels guilty after running over a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret is to feel sorry about something done, a verb synonym for repenting.

clue.text: Ducks seen outside harbour town and city

indicators.note: seen outside means the letters for ducks wrap around the other word

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two Os
a port is a harbour town

explanation.surface: Ducks spotted on the edge of a harbour town and a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, Portugal's second city.

clue.text: Slip catch turned game

indicators.note: turned means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a slip is a lapse or sin
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: A cricket catch in the slips turns the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip catch' is a cricket phrase, but here slip is SIN and catch is NET, and 'turned' gives TENNIS from SINNET.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a game.

clue.text: Lazy people in vain occupying property

indicators.note: occupying means the phrase for in vain sits inside the word for property

parts.note: goods are property, possessions
doing something for nothing is doing it in vain

explanation.surface: Idlers squatting in a property to no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-for-nothings are idle, worthless people, layabouts.

clue.text: See 9
Fish for any number stored in shed

indicators.note: stored in means the number letter is placed inside the shed word

parts.note: a hut is a shed
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: Fishing for any number of items stored in a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish for something is to seek or search for it, which is to hunt for it.

clue.text: Fragrant resin found in diesel emissions

indicators.note: found in means the letters are contained within the words diesel emissions

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling resin detected in exhaust fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Failure to concentrate missing out at end

indicators.note: missing out means the two letters of the word at are left out

parts.note: inattention is a failure to concentrate

explanation.surface: Losing focus means missing out at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' looks like part of 'at end' but stands alone as the definition, meaning aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a goal or purpose, as in 'ends and means', so it is a synonym for aim.
